text:
incident-bot: [INC-2026-04-12] Resolved - routing error impacting Hosted API generation endpoints (11:23 - 11:58 UTC). Severity: S2. Creating follow-up thread in #customer-success for customer communications and timeline.

Jordan: quick follow-up — root cause was a routing rule regression after yesterday's autoscaler tweak. Requests for a subset of model families were routed to a deprecated pool that hit an internal validation error, cascading into 503s. We reverted the routing change at 11:40 UTC and then restarted the pool; full recovery by 11:58.

Alex: ok. can we get a short customer-facing summary? need to know if Dedicated customers were affected or only Hosted. Also flag any potential data exposure?

Jordan: Dedicated capacity not affected — routing policy only applied to shared hosted pool. No data exfiltration risk; error was config mismatch leading to validation failures.

Priya: I can draft an email. Want to include timeline + what we did to mitigate + preventative actions. Also want to offer a small credit for impacted customers — any guidance on credit amount?

Maria: recommend standard goodwill: 5% credit for the billing window during the outage for Hosted customers who saw >= 5% error rate. We should coordinate with finance to finalize.

Sam: FYI support queue saw ~42 customers open tickets referencing errors between 11:25-12:15 UTC. I'll attach the exported list. We should avoid promising SLA credits until finance signs off.

Alex: here's a first-pass customer email. please edit for tone.

Priya: love this. tightening language and softening technical bits. also removing the sentence that mentions specific internal pool names.

Jordan: posting technical timeline for the RCA section — please check accuracy.

Jordan: ```
Technical timeline (UTC)
- 11:23 Detect: Spike in 503s observed by synthetic monitors and customer reports.
- 11:27 Alerting: On-call page and incident-bot created incident.
- 11:30 Triage: Confirmed increased 503s correlated with routing rules rolled out at 02:00 UTC.
- 11:35 Mitigation 1: Scoped rollback of the most recent routing change. Error rate dropped ~30% after rollback.
- 11:40 Mitigation 2: Restarted affected worker pool to clear validation errors.
- 11:58 Recovery: Error rate returned to baseline.
- 12:05 Post-checks: Ran synthetic checks across model families, verified Dedicated unaffected.
```

Alex: that looks good. Add sentence that we have an open follow-up to add automated validation to the routing rollout process.

Priya: draft customer email v2 (edited):

Priya: ```
Hi there,

We want to let you know about a temporary disruption to Redwood Hosted API that occurred on 2026-04-12 between approximately 11:23 and 11:58 UTC. During this window some customers experienced increased 5xx errors when calling generation endpoints.

What happened
- A recent routing configuration change caused a subset of requests to be directed to an incompatible worker pool, resulting in elevated 5xx responses for affected calls.
- Dedicated and private deployments were not impacted.

What we did\- We reverted the configuration and restarted the affected workers, restoring normal service by 11:58 UTC.
- We validated recovery with automated checks across model families.

What we are doing next\- We are implementing additional rollout validations and a canary gating step for routing changes to prevent this class of regression.
- We will follow up with any customers who reported sustained issues during the window.

If you were impacted, our support team will reach out with next steps, and we will consider a goodwill credit where appropriate.

We apologize for the disruption and appreciate your patience.

— Redwood Inference Operations
```

Maria: wording looks good. suggest adding a one-line "no data exposure" statement.

Priya: updated line: "There is no evidence of data exposure or exfiltration related to this incident."

Sam: support will queue that email as a template and send to the impacted list after finance confirms credits. I'll hold send until we have the final CC list.

Alex: proposed status page update (short):

Alex: "Resolved — routing configuration regression caused elevated 5xx errors for Hosted API generation endpoints between 11:23–11:58 UTC UTC. Full service restored by 11:58 UTC. Root cause: regression in routing rollout; remediation: rollback and worker restart. Follow-up: rollout validation improvements planned."

Maria: add link to customer RCAs when available. maybe include incident ID.

Jordan: can we get a quick approval on the customer email + status page so CS can proceed?

Priya: I approve the email copy with the data exposure sentence and the softened technical bits.

Alex: I approve the status page text.

Maria: finance — please advise on credit approach. tagging @finance in thread (separate message).

incident-bot: Note: scheduled postmortem meeting created for 2026-04-13 16:00 UTC (invite sent).

Sam: action items I'm tracking: export impacted customer list (done), hold template until finance sign-off, send outbound to affected customers once approved.

Jordan: action items from eng: implement gating validation for routing rollouts (P0 follow-up), add synthetic checks for early detection of routing mismatches, and document mitigation playbook. Est. initial PR in 48 hours.

Alex: I'll draft the postmortem section for the internal RCA doc and share link here when ready.

Priya: final check — who will actually press send on the customer outbound? Sam?

Sam: yes, I'll send once finance confirms credits. please DM me any customers who need bespoke language.

Priya: thanks everyone. cc'ing the incident thread into the internal RCA doc for completeness. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Page update published to status.redwood.ai at 13:03 UTC.

Jordan: closing the follow-up thread here; will post the finalized RCA doc link in this thread when ready.

Priya: thanks — marking as resolved from CS side.

Sam: leaving a note in the ticketing system summarizing outreach plan.

Alex: good work all.
